title: Light Sport Aircraft Insurance After MOSAIC: What Sport Pilots and LSA Owners Need to Know in 2026
description: Light sport aircraft insurance after the FAA MOSAIC rule: what sport pilots can fly, S-LSA vs E-LSA cover, ultralights, and the questions to ask at renewal.
author: Insurance Bhaiya Research Desk
keyTakeaways: The FAA's **MOSAIC** rule expanded sport pilot privileges on **October 22, 2025**, and replaced the old LSA definition with a performance-based light-sport category on **July 24, 2026**.
Sport pilots can now fly airplanes with up to a **59-knot stall speed** (clean), **four-seat** airframes (one passenger only), and, with endorsements, retractable gear and constant-speed props.

Insurers have said cover continues for sport pilots flying within their FAA privileges, but **conditions may be added case by case at renewal**. Disclose any new aircraft type to your insurer before flying it.
Factory-built **S-LSA** and kit-built **E-LSA** are underwritten differently. E-LSA follows many [experimental aircraft insurance](/learn/experimental-aircraft-insurance/) rules.

faqs.question: Can a sport pilot get insurance for a four-seat airplane after MOSAIC?
faqs.answer: Possibly, if the aircraft meets the 59-knot clean stall limit and the insurer's pilot warranty is satisfied. Expect make-and-model training requirements. See [aircraft & aviation insurance explained](/learn/aircraft-aviation-insurance-explained/).

faqs.question: Is light sport aircraft insurance cheaper?
faqs.answer: Usually, because hull values are lower. The hull rate and pilot-experience factors work the same way as for certified aircraft.

faqs.question: Can you insure a Part 103 ultralight?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the market is small and cover is often liability only.

content.text: Light sport aviation has always been the cheaper way into flying: a driver's license instead of a medical certificate, 20 hours minimum training for an airplane, and lighter, simpler aircraft. The FAA's MOSAIC rule has now expanded what counts as light sport and what a sport pilot can fly. Insurance terms are adjusting to those changes. This spoke of our [aircraft & aviation insurance explained](/learn/aircraft-aviation-insurance-explained/) hub covers what has changed and what hasn't.

rows: 1,320 lb max gross (1,430 seaplane), 45-kt stall, 120-kt max
Performance-based: up to 61 KCAS stall (flaps), 250 KCAS max, no weight limit (from July 24, 2026)
Up to 59 KCAS clean stall; four-seaters with one passenger (from Oct 22, 2025)
Fixed gear, fixed-pitch or ground-adjustable prop
Retractable gear and constant-speed props with endorsements

content.title: New Privileges ≠ Automatic Coverage
content.text: Being legal to fly an older four-seat Cessna as a sport pilot doesn't mean your insurer will cover you in it. The pilot warranty still sets minimum hours and time in type. Tell your insurer before flying any aircraft type you haven't flown before. For Cessna-specific pricing, see [Cessna insurance](/qa/cessna-insurance/). Any change of aircraft or pilot should be added by [insurance endorsement](/learn/what-is-an-insurance-endorsement/), not just a phone call.
S-LSA vs E-LSA vs Ultralight Insurance

items: **S-LSA (special, factory-built):** Can be used for rental and flight training. Underwritten much like certified trainers, with standard hull and liability.

**E-LSA (experimental, kit- or plans-built):** Limited to sport, recreation and instruction of the owner. Underwriters look at build quality and documentation, as covered in [experimental aircraft insurance](/learn/experimental-aircraft-insurance/).
**Part 103 ultralights:** No FAA pilot certificate or aircraft registration is required, and fewer insurers write them. Cover is often liability only, sometimes through ultralight associations.

content.text: Hull is still written at an agreed value. Light sport aircraft have lower values than four-seat certified singles, so total premiums are usually lower too. The rate mechanics are the same as in [airplane insurance cost](/learn/airplane-insurance-cost/). The details of what hull cover pays are in [what does aircraft hull insurance cover](/qa/what-does-aircraft-hull-insurance-cover/). Sport pilots who rent should still carry [private pilot insurance](/qa/private-pilot-insurance/), and those sharing an LSA should read [aircraft partnership insurance](/qa/aircraft-partnership-insurance/). Light sport seaplanes have their own water-operation risks. See [seaplane insurance](/learn/seaplane-insurance/).

content.title: Flying on a Driver's License? Plan for Medical Changes
content.text: Sport pilots don't need an FAA medical, but life and disability underwriters will still ask about aviation. See [does life insurance cover private pilots](/qa/does-life-insurance-cover-private-pilots/) before you apply for a new life policy.
